edges: The case cites that attorney-client privilege did not protect attorneys' summaries of clients' business transactions.

multi_hop_neighbors.edge: An attorney may represent a new client against a former client only if no confidential information relevant to the new representation is received from the former client.
The attorney has a duty of disclosure which is crucial in bankruptcy cases.
Attorneys protect themselves by putting the agreements in writing.
The attorney and client have an agreement regarding the scope of representation.
The court may impose sanctions on an attorney for willfully disregarding fiduciary obligations under disclosure rules.
